items.rationale: The context window holds everything sent for the call (system prompt, tool definitions, messages including tool results) plus the output. Picking d shows M3, that the model stores past conversations itself.
Each step is a separate model call, and the program sends the history again with each call. Picking a shows M3, that the model remembers by itself.
Retrieval is done by the program or a tool, which selects the relevant pages and loads them; the model sees only what is loaded. Picking b shows M6.
Context is re-sent on every call, so a pasted manual is paid for six times per request, and more context can reduce recall (context rot). Picking a, b or c invents limits that do not exist.

Compaction summarizes a conversation nearing the limit and starts a new window with the summary; structured notes are written to storage outside the window and loaded back later. Picking b shows M5, that memory is automatic and inside the model.
